claims.text: SPS-processed W–Cu compacts often contain voids and imperfect W–Cu interfaces.
Mechanical alloying before SPS will improve interparticle bonding relative to SPS without mechanical alloying.
Mechanical alloying before SPS will reduce void formation relative to processing without the alloying step.
Mechanical alloying increases the surface reactivity of W and Cu particles.
The increased surface reactivity produced by mechanical alloying promotes transient liquid-phase bonding during SPS.
Transient liquid-phase bonding during SPS improves particle contact and minimizes void formation.
Mechanical alloying refines particle surfaces and creates more active W–Cu interfaces.
During rapid, pulsed SPS, mechanically activated surfaces enhance interdiffusion and bonding between W and Cu.
Enhanced W–Cu interdiffusion and bonding reduce voids and phase separation.
Voids and phase separation impair thermal transport in W–Cu composites.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will produce a more uniform W–Cu microstructure than Cu infiltration or SPS without prior mechanical alloying.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will reduce porosity relative to Cu infiltration or SPS without prior mechanical alloying.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will improve thermal conductivity relative to Cu infiltration or SPS without prior mechanical alloying.
The proposed process will preserve the mechanical durability required for fusion-reactor applications.
The proposed mechanism and outcomes can be realized using SPS temperatures of approximately 1050–1200 °C and powder sizes of 5–50 μm.
The process is applicable to W–Cu fusion-reactor joint components exposed to irradiation service conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires mechanical durability to be preserved, whereas the falsification rule requires durability to be enhanced. A result that preserves but does not enhance durability would satisfy the prediction yet be declared falsifying.
